A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete and readable, including their appendices. Despite substantial retitling and refocusing, they share the GP-to-state-space construction, neural recording session, and matching regression results, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original kernel covariance and regression experiments, PM10 regression results, and neural latent-variable analysis in Tables 2–4, Figure 1, and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports synthetic delay recovery and two-region and five-region neural experiments in Figures 1–3, retained regression results in Appendix D, and additional analyses in Appendices C, E, and F.

M1.justification: v2 introduces ADM with time-varying MOSE delays and transition/noise matrices, plus parallel scan Kalman EM inference (Sections 2.3–3). Equation 11 also changes the augmented process-noise block from zeros to an identity matrix. The across-region/within-region latent decomposition itself already appeared in v1 Section 5.3 and Appendix H.

E1.justification: v2 adds synthetic time-varying neural communication recovery and recordings from five mouse visual regions. It retains the same V1–V2 recording session and nine kernel regression cases, but removes the London PM10 task and Periodic-kernel evaluation.

E2.justification: The retained regression comparisons lose M-GP-SF, leaving GP versus the renamed SSM-Approx. v2 adds MRM-GP alongside DLAG in the two-region comparison and evaluates mDLAG in the five-region comparison (Figures 2–3). The removed PM10 experiment also eliminates its SGPR comparisons.

E3.justification: The neural split changes from 75%/25% training/testing to 80%/10%/10% training/validation/testing. v2 adds validation-based order selection and five-region grid search, and constructs timing sequences by concatenating trials rather than changing bin size. Retained regression settings change P from 8 to 2 for SE and LMC, and from 8 to 4 for RQ; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix A's P/N sensitivity analyses for covariance error and PM10 performance disappear. v2 adds neural likelihood sensitivity to P, sequential-versus-parallel timing analysis, and regionwise factor-analysis curves for latent-size selection. The sample-smoothness analysis changes from SM to MOSE, and additional latent/delay plots extend the neural case studies.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports neural test likelihood averaged over five random seeds and synthetic delay variance across five runs; v1's neural experiment did not specify its run count. Retained regression tables preserve their uncertainty values but omit v1's five-random-splits caption. These are reporting changes, without evidence of an increased run count.

E6.justification: The nine retained GP and proposed-method regression MSE entries match exactly, including uncertainty values. Covariance, regression nLL, Periodic-kernel, and PM10 results are removed. New results show dynamic-delay recovery and higher neural test likelihood than MRM-GP/DLAG and mDLAG within v2's comparisons. Its changing forward/feedback patterns replace v1's static feedback findings; changed models and protocols prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 formally extends the model to time-dependent delays and state-space matrices while keeping length scales fixed, and revises the augmented noise covariance. It removes v1 Appendix D's continuous-time SDE, spectral-factorization, and separable multi-output derivations. The central covariance and Cholesky derivations, and most EM algebra, remain through relocation to Appendices A–B.

C1.justification: v1 centers on universal stationary GP conversion with linear computation and accurate covariance/regression approximation. v2 retains the universal connection claim but centers its abstract, introduction, and discussion on continuously changing multi-region communication, concurrent delays without discrete hidden states, and O(log T) parallel inference.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes agreement in delay signs and discusses periodic-kernel discrepancies, SGPR bottlenecks, and stationary/temporal-input restrictions. v2 interprets evolving delay magnitudes through communication speed, prediction error, synchronization, inhibition, and visual hierarchy. Its limitations discussion instead emphasizes cubic scaling with region count and model order and possible frequency-domain remedies.

D1.justification: v1 Appendices F–G specify kernel parameters, amplitude coefficients, hardware, epochs, learning rates, optimizers, and libraries. Much of this reproducibility information is absent from v2, including corresponding neural training details. v2 adds neuron counts, stimulus and smoothing descriptions, the five-region session identifier, and model-selection settings; Cholesky implementation guidance survives in Appendix A.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts from general GP conversion and scalable GP methods toward neural communication models and parallel inference. v2 adds substantial discussion of MR-SDS, mp-srSLDS, mDLAG, parallel scans/smoothers, and predictive coding, while removing many conversion and sparse-GP references. MRM-GP was already cited in v1 but becomes a central design contrast and evaluated comparator.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, inference narrative, experiments, and discussion are extensively rewritten around ADM. Related work is integrated into the introduction, GPFA background moves from Appendix H into Section 2.1, and covariance derivations and retained regression experiments move into appendices. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond added scientific content.

P2.justification: The conversion-survey and PM10 tables disappear, while v1 Tables 2–3 become compact, two-method, MSE-only appendix tables. The static neural figure and covariance/sensitivity displays are replaced by dynamic-delay, network, timing, and model-selection panels, with additional appendix latent-variable figures. Both display structure and placement change extensively.

improvement.justification: v2 adds meaningful dynamic-delay capability, synthetic recovery evidence, five-region validation, and parallel-inference comparisons. However, it removes direct covariance validation and substantial training documentation while retaining the universal conversion claim. Identical regression scores accompany revised order settings, and the changed noise block in Equation 11 lacks an explanation of its effect. These gains and unresolved losses in evidential support and reproducibility prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
